## Project objective 
 
This educational project compares frequentist and Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis using published aggregate data from historic studies of BCG vaccination and tuberculosis cases. 
 
The workflow calculates study-level odds ratios, estimates pooled associations and between-study heterogeneity, assesses study influence, fits a Bayesian hierarchical model in Stan, and compares frequentist confidence intervals with Bayesian credible intervals. 
 
## Dataset 
 
The analysis used the `dat.colditz1994` dataset distributed through the R package `metadat`. 
 
The dataset contains 13 historic published studies with aggregate 2×2 event data: 
 
- tuberculosis cases in BCG-vaccinated groups; 
- participants without tuberculosis in BCG-vaccinated groups; 
- tuberculosis cases in control groups; 
- participants without tuberculosis in control groups. 
 
This is an educational re-analysis of historic published aggregate data. It is not a new systematic review, treatment recommendation, regulatory submission, or health technology assessment. 
 
## Study-level effect sizes 
 
Odds ratios were calculated for each study. 
 
An odds ratio below 1 indicates lower odds of tuberculosis cases in the BCG-vaccinated group relative to the control group within that study. 
 
## Frequentist random-effects meta-analysis 
 
A random-effects meta-analysis was fitted using restricted maximum likelihood (REML). 
 
- Studies included: 13 
- Pooled odds ratio: 0.475 
- 95% confidence interval: 0.330 to 0.683 
- Between-study variance, tau-squared: 0.338 
- I-squared: 92.1% 
 
### Forest plot 
 
![](../outputs/figures/bcg_frequentist_forest_plot.png) 
 
The pooled frequentist estimate was below 1. However, heterogeneity was high, indicating substantial variation in the study-specific estimates. 
 
## Heterogeneity and influence diagnostics 
 
Cochran's Q statistic was 163.0 with 12 degrees of freedom, with a very small p-value. This was consistent with substantial heterogeneity across studies. 
 
### Baujat plot 
 
![](../outputs/figures/bcg_baujat_plot.png) 
 
The Baujat plot showed that Study 8 (TPT Madras, 1980) had the strongest combined contribution to heterogeneity and influence on the pooled estimate. Study 4 (Hart and Sutherland, 1977) was also relatively influential. 
 
No studies were excluded solely because of these diagnostics. 
 
Leave-one-out analysis showed that the pooled odds ratio remained below 1 when each study was omitted in turn. Therefore, no individual study alone determined the direction of the pooled association. 
 
## Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis 
 
A Bayesian hierarchical random-effects model was fitted in Stan using four Markov chain Monte Carlo chains. 
 
The model estimated: 
 
- `mu`: pooled log odds ratio; 
- `tau`: between-study standard deviation on the log odds-ratio scale; 
- study-specific underlying effects. 
 
The priors were: 
 
```text 
mu ~ Normal(0, 2) 
tau ~ Half-Normal(0, 1) 
```
### MCMC diagnostics 
 
All four chains completed successfully. 
 
- R-hat values were 1.00 for the pooled effect and heterogeneity parameters. 
- Effective sample sizes were high. 
- No divergent-transition warnings were reported. 
 
These diagnostics support convergence for this model run. 
 
### Bayesian pooled effect 
 
- Posterior mean pooled odds ratio: 0.488 
- 95% credible interval: 0.315 to 0.717 
- Posterior mean tau: 0.641 
- 95% credible interval for tau: 0.373 to 1.06 
 
### Posterior distribution of pooled odds ratio 
 
![](../outputs/figures/bcg_bayesian_pooled_odds_ratio_posterior.png) 
 
The posterior distribution is concentrated below an odds ratio of 1. Under the specified model and priors, it supports lower odds of tuberculosis cases in BCG-vaccinated groups than in control groups in these historic data. 
 
### Posterior distribution of heterogeneity 
 
![](../outputs/figures/bcg_bayesian_tau_posterior.png) 
 
The posterior distribution of tau indicates substantial uncertainty and variation in underlying study effects. 
 
## Frequentist and Bayesian comparison 
 
| Method | Pooled odds ratio | Uncertainty interval | 
|---|---:|---| 
| Frequentist random-effects meta-analysis (REML) | 0.475 | 95% confidence interval: 0.330 to 0.683 | 
| Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis (Stan) | 0.488 | 95% credible interval: 0.315 to 0.717 | 
 
The frequentist and Bayesian estimates were similar. Both approaches estimated a pooled odds ratio below 1, while also indicating substantial between-study heterogeneity. 
 
## Reproducibility 
 
Run the R scripts in this order: 
 
```text 
scripts/01_install_packages.R 
scripts/02_load_bcg_data.R 
scripts/03_frequentist_random_effects_meta_analysis.R 
scripts/04_heterogeneity_and_influence_checks.R 
scripts/05_install_cmdstanr.R 
scripts/06_bayesian_random_effects_meta_analysis.R 
scripts/07_bayesian_visualisations_and_model_comparison.R 
``` 
 
The Stan model is located at: 
 
```text 
models/bayesian_random_effects_meta_analysis.stan 
``` 
 
## Limitations 
 
- This project uses historic published aggregate data from 13 studies. 
- It is not a systematic review with a prospectively registered protocol. 
- Study-level aggregate data do not allow patient-level adjustment. 
- High heterogeneity limits interpretation of a single pooled estimate. 
- The Bayesian results depend on the specified model structure and prior distributions. 
- The analysis does not assess study quality, publication bias, current BCG policy, current tuberculosis epidemiology, or clinical applicability. 
- Results are educational and must not be used for clinical or public-health decision-making. 
 
## Conclusion 
 
This project demonstrates frequentist and Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis in R and Stan. 
 
The frequentist and Bayesian models produced similar pooled odds-ratio estimates while highlighting substantial between-study heterogeneity. The project demonstrates evidence synthesis, uncertainty communication, heterogeneity assessment, Bayesian hierarchical modelling, and reproducible reporting.
